answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check and renewed periodically. The network then weights votes or payouts by verified credentials, not wallet count, so splitting control across a thousand fresh accounts gains no extra influence. An attacker must recruit real people or repeatedly defeat costly checks; buying cheap keys is not enough. Even on an island, a crystal-clear ledger and a sonnet of coordinated fake accounts cannot turn one verified identity into many.
